items.title: Pairing AIS with RF: Analysis of a Markovian Approach for Maritime Data Fusion
items.summary: The article evaluates a Markovian method that fuses AIS data with space‑based RF observations to improve maritime surveillance accuracy.
items.whyItMatters: It offers a more reliable detection of illicit maritime activity, benefiting security analysts and maritime operators.

items.title: FETTUCCINE: Fast and efficient brain-to-text decoding on mobile devices
items.summary: FETTUCCINE presents a lightweight brain‑to‑text decoder that runs efficiently on mobile devices, reducing the computational load of speech neuroprostheses.
items.whyItMatters: Tech‑savvy readers will value its low‑resource design, enabling real‑time neural communication on everyday hardware.

items.title: Training Reasoning Models in Simulation to Natively Use Real Robots
items.summary: An open-weight 27B reasoning model is trained to control real robots directly via simulation, bridging the gap between proprietary and open models.
items.whyItMatters: It enables broader, cost‑effective robot control for developers without access to proprietary AI.

items.title: BAL: Bidirectional Autoregression in Latent Space for Learning Human Movement Representations
items.summary: The paper introduces Bidirectional Autoregression in Latent Space to learn human movement representations from 3D pose sequences without relying on heuristic augmentations.
items.whyItMatters: It offers a more principled, self-supervised approach that could improve motion modeling for robotics and animation.

items.title: WeightBench: Evaluating Language Models as Weight-Space Programmers
items.summary: The paper introduces a benchmark for testing large language models that can modify neural network weights directly, a technique called Weight‑Space Programming.
items.whyItMatters: It shows LLMs can edit models without gradients, opening new ways to repair and design AI systems.

items.title: Imitation Bootstrapped Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: The paper introduces Round‑Robin Behavior Cloning, enabling a single demonstrator to train multiple agents by controlling them sequentially.
items.whyItMatters: It simplifies data collection for multi‑agent RL, speeding up training for complex cooperative tasks.

items.title: Elliptic Sampling: Optimal Interpolant Schedules for Gaussians and Beyond
items.summary: The paper proposes a framework to jointly design interpolant schedules and discretizations for stochastic interpolants using ODE trajectory analyticity.
items.whyItMatters: It could improve efficiency and accuracy in diffusion-based generative models.

items.title: Why Finite Intelligence Works in an Infinite World: A Mathematical Theory
items.summary: The article explains how finite representations can capture essential information for future tasks without modeling an infinite environment, using a mathematical framework.
items.whyItMatters: It shows efficient AI design can generalize from limited data, crucial for scalable, resource‑constrained systems.

items.title: ModHarness-RL: Recasting Harnesses as Learnable and Evolving Programs for Agentic RL
items.summary: ModHarness‑RL proposes learning and evolving harnesses—dynamic scaffolds that adapt what agents observe and how they are guided—rather than fixed hand‑written ones.
items.whyItMatters: Tech‑savvy readers see improved agent performance and adaptability by automating harness design.

items.title: Alignment by Socialization: Learning Tradeoffs Under Selection
items.summary: The paper explores how evolutionary selection influences AI agents' tradeoffs between task performance and rule compliance, assessing if experience aligns choices with human values.
items.whyItMatters: Understanding selection-driven alignment helps design AI that balances efficiency and ethics under changing conditions.

items.title: Understanding Contextual Bias in Agricultural CNNs Through Hidden-Neuron Concept Induction
items.summary: The article explores how CNNs use background context for image classification and applies Concept Induction to interpret hidden-layer representations in agricultural imagery.
items.whyItMatters: It helps tech-savvy readers understand and mitigate bias in AI models used for precision agriculture.

items.title: WaferTetris: Efficient Freeform Mapping on Wafer-Scale Accelerators
items.summary: WaferTetris introduces a new method for efficiently mapping applications onto wafer-scale accelerators, addressing challenges of programming and resource allocation.
items.whyItMatters: It could boost productivity and performance on next‑generation wafer‑scale hardware.

items.title: StreamEmbed: Real-Time Indexing from Pixels for Screenshot Retrieval
items.summary: Screen history can serve as searchable visual memory for people and agents, but unlike an offline corpus, it must be encoded and indexed as each screenshot arrives. OCR-based indexing is fast but loses visual information; visual encoding takes over two seconds. Yet screens change incrementally: most pixels repeat within and across screenshots. items.title: Can Mechanistic Interpretability Help Explain LLM Agent Failures? A Case Study on Web Element Hallucination
items.summary: Mechanistic Interpretability (MI) has made significant progress in explaining the internal computations of Large Language Models (LLMs); however, these advances have yet to demonstrate comparable success in explaining the decision-making processes of LLM-based agents. items.title: MeReader: An Offline, Privacy-Preserving, Progress-Aware AI Assistant for Narrative eBook Reading
items.summary: This paper introduces MeReader, a privacy-preserving, offline and progress-aware AI assistant designed to function as a contextual companion for narrative reading on consumer hardware. Unlike conventional Large Language Model (LLM)-based systems that process documents/books online in an all-texts-at-once type of way, thereby risking narrative spoilers, MeReader confines both retrieval and…

items.title: On numerical issues of divergences between nearly equal distributions
items.summary: Barron et al. (2026) recently identified numerical issues in the softmax and soft cross-entropy loss. We show that similar issues are present in standard divergence operations between categorical distributions. items.title: Asymptotic Margins and Feature Confinement in Conic Classification Heads under Softmax Cross-Entropy
items.summary: Classification heads built on conic functions give each class a bounded region of the feature space, and such regions are used to reject samples of unseen classes. We ask whether these regions also keep the features bounded when the head is trained with softmax cross-entropy. items.title: Agentic induction of common data elements and information extraction from sarcoma case report abstracts
items.summary: Common data elements (CDEs) support clinical data comparability but are usually defined manually. We investigated whether large language model agents could derive a CDE schema from sarcoma case report abstracts and apply it at scale. An agent proposed 72,909 candidate CDEs from 24,588 PubMed abstracts; agentic consolidation yielded 1,570 CDEs. We retained 53 supported by at least 50 abstracts and…

items.title: Agentic AI for Discovering Fault-Tolerant Quantum Circuits
items.summary: Scaling quantum computing toward practical quantum advantage is currently limited by the efficiency of circuits that operate on information encoded by quantum error-correcting codes. items.title: ARCHER: From Rationale Imitation to Executable Reasoning in Small Language Models
items.summary: Small language models are attractive for local, low-cost, and privacy-sensitive deployment, but they remain unreliable on mathematical reasoning tasks that require decomposition, exact computation, tool use, and verification.
